title.zh: 卷三十 志第二十 刑法
title.raw: 卷三十 志第二十 刑法 Volume 30 Treatises 20: Punishment and Law

sentences.zh: 刑法志

translations.literal: Treatise on Punishment and Law.
translations.idiomatic: Monograph: Criminal Law.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「齊之以禮，有恥且格。

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "When they are ordered with ritual, they will have a sense of shame and will correct themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The tradition reads: "Regulate them with ritual, and they feel shame and mend their ways.

sentences.zh: 」刑之不可犯，不若禮之不可逾，則昊歲比於犧年，宜有降矣。

translations.literal: " That punishments cannot be violated is still inferior to ritual's being impossible to transgress; then comparing the vast age with the age of sacrifice, there ought to be a lowering.
translations.idiomatic: " Fear of penalties still falls short of reverence that stops people short of breaching ritual; set beside an age of innocence, ours ought to show a lighter touch.

sentences.zh: 若夫穹圓肇判，宵貌攸分，流形播其喜怒，稟氣彰其善惡，則有自然之理焉。

translations.literal: As for when the round vault first split open and dark and bright were divided, embodied forms broadcast joy and anger and endowed qi manifests good and evil—there is a principle of nature therein.
translations.idiomatic: When heaven first divided above from below and living shapes took on joy, anger, and moral color through the qi they received, they followed patterns inherent in nature itself.

sentences.zh: 念室後刑，衢樽先惠，將以屏除災害，引導休和，取譬琴瑟，不忘銜策，擬陽秋之成化，若堯舜之為心也。

translations.literal: The chamber of reflection comes after punishment; the crossroads wine comes before kindness—they intend thereby to ward off calamity and guide toward harmony, likened to zither and se, not forgetting bit and whip, modeling the transformative completion of the Spring and Autumn, as the mind of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Thoughtful detention precedes sentence; wine offered at the crossroads signals mercy first—the aim is to banish harm and lead society toward peace, like tuning zither and zither-bass together while still holding rein and crop, in the spirit of the Spring and Autumn's moral transformation and the benevolence of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 效原布肅，軒皇有轡野之師；

translations.literal: When awe was spread across the plains, the Yellow Emperor had armies in the wilds with bridled horses;
translations.idiomatic: When the wasteland was swept with solemn dread, the Yellow Emperor led tethered hosts across the open fields.

sentences.zh: 雷電揚威，高辛有觸山之務。

translations.literal: When thunder and lightning displayed might, Gaoxin had the task of striking the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Where thunder displayed Heaven's wrath, Emperor Ku turned lightning against rebellious peaks.

sentences.zh: 陳乎兵甲而肆諸市朝，具嚴天刑，以懲亂首，論其本意，蓋有不得已而用之者焉。

translations.literal: Arraying arms and armor and exposing offenders in market and court, fully deploying stern heavenly punishment to punish the heads of chaos—in discussing their original intent, there were probably those who had no choice but to use it.
translations.idiomatic: They displayed weapons, executed ringleaders in the marketplace and at court, and invoked awe-inspiring punishments because, at bottom, some crises left rulers no alternative.

sentences.zh: 是以丹浦興仁，羽山咸服。

translations.literal: Therefore at Danpi kindness arose, and at Yushan all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Hence kindness rose from the banks of Dan, and submission reached even banishment at Mount Yu.

sentences.zh: 而世屬僥倖，事關攸蠹，政失禮微，獄成刑起，則孔子曰：「聽訟吾猶人也，必也使無訟乎！

translations.literal: But when the age belongs to the lucky, affairs touch what gnaws within, government loses ritual and grows faint, prisons are completed and punishments arise, then Confucius said: "In hearing lawsuits I am like other men; surely I must make it so there are no lawsuits!
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever fortune favors the reckless, institutions rot within, governance slackens, ritual fades, and prisons swell, Confucius complained: "I decide cases no better than anyone—what I want is an end to litigation altogether!

sentences.zh: 」及周氏龔行，卻收鋒刃，祖述生成，憲章堯禹，政有膏露，威兼禮樂，或觀辭以明其趣，或傾耳以照其微，或彰善以激其情，或除惡以崇其本。

translations.literal: " When the house of Zhou marched to punish evil, they put away blades and edges, taking their model from nurturing life, taking Yao and Yu as their constitution; government had the dew of kindness, awe embraced ritual and music; sometimes observing words to clarify their intent, sometimes inclining the ear to illumine subtleties, sometimes displaying good to stir feelings, sometimes removing evil to elevate the root.
translations.idiomatic: " Later the Zhou armies marched under Heaven's mandate, sheathed the sword, honored nurture and growth, and modeled themselves on Yao and Yu—government tasted sweet as dew, majesty paired with ritual and music; rulers listened to petitions, caught whispered grievances, praised virtue to encourage it, and purged wickedness to protect the moral core.

sentences.zh: 至夫取威定霸，一匡九合，寓言成康，不由凝網，此所謂酌其遺美，而愛民治國者焉。

translations.literal: As for securing awe and fixing hegemony, uniting and correcting the realm in nine assemblies, allegorically pointing to Cheng and Kang, not relying on a tightening net—this is what is called drawing on their surviving excellence and loving the people and governing the state.
translations.idiomatic: Those who forged prestige, stabilized hegemony, unified the regional lords, and invoked the peace of Kings Cheng and Kang without leaning on harsh nets drank from that legacy of mercy—true governance that cherishes the people.

sentences.zh: 若乃化蔑彝倫，道睽明慎，則夏癸之虔劉百姓，商辛之毒{疒甫}四海，衛鞅之無所自容，韓非之不勝其虐，與夫《甘棠》流詠，未或同歸。

translations.literal: But when transformation scorns constant norms and the Way parts from clarity and care, then Jie of Xia's slaughtering the hundred surnames, Zhou of Shang's poisoning and afflicting the four seas, Shang Yang having nowhere to hide himself, Han Fei's cruelty beyond bearing—with the flowing praise of Sweet Pear they share no common end.
translations.idiomatic: When rulers mock moral order and abandon cautious justice, you get Jie slaughtering his subjects, Zhou sinking his cruelty across the realm, Shang Yang with nowhere honorable to stand, Han Fei drowned in his own harsh doctrines—nothing like the ode to the sweet pear tree where the people still sang of kindness.

sentences.zh: 秦文初造參夷，始皇加之抽協，囹圄如市，悲哀盈路。

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Qin first created triple-extinction punishment; the First Emperor added tearing ribs apart; prisons were like markets; grief filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's Duke Wen invented kin-extinction statutes; the First Emperor piled on flaying and rib-tearing torments until jails looked like busy markets and wailing clogged every road.

sentences.zh: 漢王以三章之法以吊之，文帝以刑厝之道以臨之，于時百姓欣然，將逢交泰。

translations.literal: The King of Han used the three-chapter law to console them; Emperor Wen used the approach of laying punishments aside to oversee them; at that time the hundred surnames were pleased, about to meet intertwining peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Han founder soothed the realm with three simple articles; Emperor Wen governed by storing the axe away; ordinary families tasted relief and hoped for an era of perfect harmony.

sentences.zh: 而犴逐情遷，科隨意往，獻瓊杯于闕下，徙青衣于蜀路，覆醢裁刑，傾宗致獄。

translations.literal: Yet as prison gates yielded to shifting passions and statutes followed shifting intent, jade cups were offered below the palace gates and blue-clad convicts were moved to Shu roads; overturning the pickle tub decided punishment, toppling clans brought prosecution.
translations.idiomatic: Soon passions swayed verdicts, statutes bent to whim, poison wine waited below the palace stair, convicts in blue were marched toward Shu, summary executions overturned justice, and whole lineages were dragged into court.

sentences.zh: 況乃數囚於京兆之夜，五日于長安之市，北闕相引、中都繼及者，亦往往而有焉。

translations.literal: Moreover counting prisoners on nights in the capital district, five days in Chang'an market—those linked from the northern gate and reaching to the central capital—often occurred as well.
translations.idiomatic: Night sweeps hauled suspects through the capital; Chang'an's market hosted staggered executions for days on end; indictments chained together from the northern gate through the inner metropolis became grimly routine.

sentences.zh: 而將亡之國，典刑咸棄，刊章以急其憲，適意以寬其網，桓靈之季，不其然歟！

translations.literal: And in states about to perish, canonical punishments were all abandoned; engraved statutes hurried their statutes; indulgent intent widened their net—in the twilight of Huan and Ling, was it not so!
translations.idiomatic: Dying dynasties tossed precedent aside, rushed new prohibitions onto the books, and loosened the net whenever it suited them—look no further than the chaos under Emperors Huan and Ling.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝時，宮室盛興，而期會迫急，有稽限者，帝親召問，言猶在口，身首已分。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming of Wei's time, palace construction flourished and deadlines for assemblies were pressing; those who missed the deadline—the emperor personally summoned and questioned them; while the words were still on their lips, body and head were already separated.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei Mingdi palace works multiplied, court deadlines turned lethal, and anyone who missed a roster summons faced the emperor's own interrogation—often mid-sentence the axe had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 王肅抗疏曰：「陛下之所行刑，皆宜死之人也。

translations.literal: Wang Su submitted a memorial resisting: "Those whom Your Majesty executes all deserve death.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su protested in a memorial: "Everyone you execute deserves death.

sentences.zh: 然眾庶不知，將為倉卒，願陛下下之于吏而暴其罪。

translations.literal: Yet the multitude does not know and will take it as hasty; I beg Your Majesty to hand them down to officials and expose their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd cannot see that and will think these deaths abrupt; please remand each case to the judiciary and publish the offenses publicly.

sentences.zh: 均其死也，不汙宮掖，不為搢紳驚惋，不為遠近所疑。

translations.literal: Equalizing their deaths, the inner palace is not defiled, the gentry are not startled and grieved, and near and far are not suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: They still die, yet the harem stays unstained, officials are spared shock, and no one far or near questions the justice of it.

sentences.zh: 人命至重，難生易殺，氣絕而不續者也，是以聖王重之。

translations.literal: Human life is supremely important—hard to live, easy to kill; once breath is cut off it does not continue—therefore sage kings prize it.
translations.idiomatic: A single life weighs more than anything: restoring it is hard, taking it is easy, and once the breath stops there is no second chance—hence sage rulers handle executions with dread.

sentences.zh: 孟軻云：'殺一不辜而取天下者，仁者不為也。'」

translations.literal: Meng Ke said: 'To kill one innocent and thereby take the empire—benevolent men will not do it.'"
translations.idiomatic: Mencius warned that no humane man seizes the realm over a single wrongful death."

sentences.zh: 世祖武皇帝接三統之微，酌千年之範，乃命有司，大明刑憲。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, our dynastic founder, took up the subtle threads of the Three Systems, drew from the models of a thousand years, then ordered the responsible offices to greatly clarify punishments and statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin caught the fading rhythm of the Three Ages, distilled a millennium of precedent, and charged his ministers to cast clear light on the criminal code.

sentences.zh: 于時詔書頒新法於天下，海內同軌，人甚安之。

translations.literal: At that time edicts promulgated the new law throughout the realm; within the seas all followed one track, and people greatly rested secure in it.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial writ spread the new code from border to border; the kingdom rolled forward on a single standard and the people breathed easier.

sentences.zh: 條綱雖設，稱為簡惠，仰昭天眷，下濟民心，道有法而無敗，德俟刑而久立。

translations.literal: Although articles and headings were set up, they were called simple and kind; above they displayed Heaven's favor, below they aided the people's hearts; the Way had law and did not fail; virtue waited upon punishments and stood long.
translations.idiomatic: The statutes looked intricate yet earned a reputation for simplicity and mercy, reflecting Heaven's care above and steadying hearts below—good order needs laws that do not rot, and lasting virtue still relies on measured punishments.

sentences.zh: 及晉圖南徙，百有二年，仰止前規，挹其流潤，江左無外，蠻陬來格。

translations.literal: When Jin's plan turned south and migrated, for one hundred two years they looked up and stopped at prior norms, drew from their flowing moisture; east of the river there was no outsider, and remote barbarians came to be corrected.
translations.idiomatic: After the court crossed the Yangzi it spent a hundred and two years gazing back at old precedents and drinking from their lingering kindness—the lower Yangzi stayed inwardly secure and frontier peoples routinely sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 孝武時，會稽王道子傾弄朝權，其所樹之黨，貨官私獄，烈祖惛迷，不聞司敗，晉之綱紀大亂焉。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xiaowu's time, Sima Daozi, Prince of Kuaiji, overturned and toyed with court power; the cliques he planted sold offices and ran private prisons; the august ancestor was dazed and confused, did not hear of judicial defeat; Jin's guiding cords were greatly disordered.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu, Prince Sima Daozi of Kuaiji twisted the government in his favor: his creatures traded posts for cash and ran private jails while Emperor Xiaowu drifted in a stupor, deaf to legal breakdown, and Jin's discipline collapsed.

sentences.zh: 傳曰「三皇設言而民不違，五帝畫象而民知禁」，則《書》所謂「象以典刑，流宥五刑，鞭作官刑，撲作教刑」者也。

translations.literal: The Commentary says, "The Three Sovereigns established words and the people did not disobey; the Five Emperors painted images and the people knew prohibition"—then this is what the Document means by "model with the canonical punishments, commute and forgive the five punishments, the whip becomes official punishment, the rod becomes instructional punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Tradition claims the Three August Ones needed only proclamations and the Five Emperors only painted warnings—exactly the ideal described in the Documents where symbolic punishments, commuting sentences, and dividing whip strokes between court and school kept order without cruelty.

sentences.zh: 然則犯黥者皁其巾，犯劓者丹其服，犯臏者墨其體，犯宮者雜其屢，大辟之罪，殊刑之極，布其衣裾而無領緣，投之於市，與眾棄之。

translations.literal: Thus those who committed branding wore black on their caps; those who committed nose-cutting reddened their garments; those who committed kneecap removal inked their bodies; those who committed castration mixed their shoes; for capital crimes, the utmost of distinctive punishments—spread their robes without collar edges, cast them into the market, abandoned them with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Branding meant a dark kerchief, clipped nose a scarlet tunic, severed knee dark markings, castration mismatched shoes, and execution—the crown of penalties—meant plain sackcloth without borders before the crowds cast you out in the square.

sentences.zh: 舜命皋陶曰；

translations.literal: Shun commanded Gao Yao, saying;
translations.idiomatic: Shun told Minister Gao Yao:

sentences.zh: 「五刑有服，五服三就，五流有宅，五宅三居。

translations.literal: "The five punishments have submission; the five submissions have three placements; the five banishments have dwellings; the five dwellings have three residences.
translations.idiomatic: "The five punishments each carried fixed gradations; those gradations determined three kinds of enforcement; banishment likewise came with paired estates and three grades of exile.

sentences.zh: 」方乎前載，事既參倍。

translations.literal: " Compared with former records, affairs were already tripled.
translations.idiomatic: " Stack that against earlier ages and the caseload had already tripled.

sentences.zh: 夏後氏之王天下也，則五刑之屬三千。

translations.literal: When the house of Xia ruled the realm, the categories of the five punishments were three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xia kings the five punishments spawned three thousand enumerated offenses.

sentences.zh: 殷因于夏，有所損益。

translations.literal: Yin inherited from Xia, having some reductions and additions.
translations.idiomatic: Shang revised the Xia code, trimming here and tightening there.

sentences.zh: 周人以三典刑邦國，以五聽察民情，左嘉右肺，事均熔造，而五刑之屬猶有二千五百焉。

translations.literal: The Zhou used three canons to punish states, used five hearings to observe the people's feelings; the complaint stone on the left, the redress stone on the right; affairs balanced in smelting and forging—yet the categories of the five punishments still numbered two thousand five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou judges relied on three penal canons and five methods of listening, with peasants pounding the left stone for grief and the right for appeals—justice forged like metal—yet the statute book still listed twenty-five hundred capital-linked clauses.

sentences.zh: 乃置三刺、三宥、三赦之法：一刺曰訊群臣，再刺曰訊群吏，三刺曰訊萬民；

translations.literal: Then they established the methods of three inquiries, three forgivings, three pardons: first inquiry called questioning the host of ministers; second inquiry called questioning the host of clerks; third inquiry called questioning the myriad people;
translations.idiomatic: They layered three rounds of consultation—first ministers, then bureaucrats, finally commoners—plus three grounds for mercy and three kinds of pardon.

sentences.zh: 一宥曰不識，再宥曰過失，三宥曰遺忘；

translations.literal: first forgiving called ignorance, second forgiving called accident, third forgiving called forgetfulness;
translations.idiomatic: Ignorance of law, honest mistake, or simple forgetfulness each earned a step down in severity.

sentences.zh: 一赦曰幼弱，再赦曰老旄，三赦曰蠢愚。

translations.literal: first pardon called young and weak, second pardon called old and hoary, third pardon called dull and foolish.
translations.idiomatic: Youth, extreme age, or congenital incapacity opened the door to commutation.

sentences.zh: 《司馬法》：或起甲兵以征不義，廢貢職則討，不朝會則誅，亂嫡庶則縶，變禮刑則放。

translations.literal: The Sima Methods: sometimes raise arms to punish the unjust; if tribute duties are abandoned then punish; if one does not attend court assemblies then execute; if legitimate and illegitimate heirs are confused then bind; if ritual and punishments are altered then banish.
translations.idiomatic: The Methods of the Minister of War authorized campaigns against oath-breakers: withhold tribute and face expedition, skip league meetings and face execution, scramble succession and face arrest, meddle with ritual penalties and face exile.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「殷周之質，不勝其文。

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "The plainness of Yin and Zhou could not bear their refinement.
translations.idiomatic: The chronicles add that Shang and Zhou began austere but drowned in ornament.

sentences.zh: 」及昭後徂征，穆王斯耄，爰制刑辟，以詰四方，奸宄弘多，亂離斯永，則所謂「夏有亂政而作《禹刑》，商有亂政而作《湯刑》，周有亂政而作《九刑》」者也。

translations.literal: " When after Zhao the king marched to punish, King Mu was thus aged; then they made punishments and laws to interrogate the four directions; villains were greatly many; disorder and separation were long—then this is what is called "Xia had disorderly government and therefore made the Yu Punishments; Shang had disorderly government and therefore made the Tang Punishments; Zhou had disorderly government and therefore made the Nine Punishments."
translations.idiomatic: " Later campaigns exhausted the kings until aging King Mu codified new statutes to rein in the provinces—each spike in crime produced its own compendium, the very "Yu," "Tang," and "Nine Punishments" named whenever dynastic order frayed.

sentences.zh: 古者大刑用甲兵，中刑用刀鋸，薄刑用鞭撲。

translations.literal: In antiquity great punishments used armor and weapons; middle punishments used knife and saw; light punishments used whip and flogging.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity reserved armies for the gravest crimes, blades and saws for middling offenses, whips and rods for the lightest.

sentences.zh: 自茲厥後，狙詐彌繁。

translations.literal: From this onward, cunning and deceit grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward schemes multiplied faster than the law could track.

sentences.zh: 武皇帝並以為往憲猶疑，不可經國，乃命車騎將軍、守尚書令、魯公徵求英俊，刊律定篇云爾。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu altogether considered that past statutes still had doubts and could not order the state; then he ordered the chariot-and-cavalry general, acting director of the Secretariat, Duke of Lu, to gather outstanding men, carve the statutes and fix the chapters—thus.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu decided Han-Wei precedent was too muddled to govern by and ordered the chariot general, acting Secretariat chief, and Duke of Lu to recruit jurists and engrave a definitive code—that story follows.

sentences.zh: 漢自王莽篡位之後，舊章不存。

translations.literal: Han after Wang Mang usurped the throne, old regulations did not survive.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Mang seized the Han throne, the classical statutes barely survived.

sentences.zh: 光武中興，留心庶獄，常臨朝聽訟，躬決疑事。

translations.literal: Guangwu's restoration, he attended to the multitude of lawsuits, often entered court to hear litigation, personally decided doubtful matters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu revived the dynasty with relentless attention to criminal justice—he held dawn audiences to hear appeals and settled knotty cases himself.

sentences.zh: 是時承離亂之後，法網弛縱，罪名既輕，無以懲肅。

translations.literal: At this time inheriting after separation and chaos, the net of law was lax; offense names were already light—there was nothing wherewith to punish and awe.
translations.idiomatic: Coming straight from civil war, the statutes hung slack; penalties felt mild and no longer terrified wrongdoers.

sentences.zh: 梁統乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: Liang Tong then submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Minister Liang Tong therefore presented this memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣竊見元帝初元五年，輕殊刑三十四事，哀帝建平元年盡四年，輕殊死者刑八十一事，其四十二事，手殺人皆減死罪一等，著為常法。

translations.literal: Your servant has privately seen that in Emperor Yuan's fifth year of Chuyuan, thirty-four matters lightened capital punishment; from Emperor Ai's first year of Jianping through the fourth year, eighty-one matters lightened punishment for capital crimes; of these forty-two matters, hand-killing persons all had death crimes reduced one grade, recorded as standing practice.
translations.idiomatic: I note that in Yuandi's Chuyuan 5 thirty-four provisions softened capital sentences, and from Aidi's Jianping 1 through Jianping 4 eighty-one more did the same—forty-two of them cutting murderers one notch below death and locking that relief into permanent precedent.

sentences.zh: 自是以後，人輕犯法，吏易殺人，吏民俱失，至於不羈。

translations.literal: From this afterward, people lightly violated the law; clerks easily killed people; clerks and commoners both lost control, to the point of being unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: After that, townsfolk shrugged at statutes, bailiffs reached for the blade too readily, officials and subjects alike abandoned restraint, and order unraveled.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為刑罰不苟務輕，務其中也。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly considers that punishments should not lightly pursue lightness; they should pursue hitting the center.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that penal policy must never chase leniency for its own sake—it must aim at true proportion.

sentences.zh: 君人之道，仁義為主，仁者愛人，義者理務。

translations.literal: The way of ruling men takes benevolence and righteousness as lord; the benevolent cherishes people; the righteous orders affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Governing rests on humanity and duty: humanity cherishes lives, duty puts affairs in order.

sentences.zh: 愛人故當為除害，理務亦當為去亂。

translations.literal: Cherishing people therefore ought to remove harm; ordering affairs likewise ought to remove chaos.
translations.idiomatic: To love the people you remove predators; to keep affairs straight you purge turmoil.

sentences.zh: 是以五帝有流殛放殺之誅，三王有大辟刻肌之刑，所以為除殘去亂也。

translations.literal: Therefore the Five Emperors had the executions of exile, throwing into abyss, banishment, and killing; the Three Kings had capital punishments that carved flesh—these served to remove cruelty and remove chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Five Legendary rulers wielded exile, drowning, banishment, and execution, while the Three Dynasties kings retained mutilating capital sentences—all to extirpate brutality and chaos.

sentences.zh: 故孔子稱「仁者必有勇」，又曰「理財正辭，禁人為非曰義」。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius praised "the benevolent necessarily has courage," and also said "ordering wealth and correcting speech, forbidding people from wrong—this is called righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius insisted that humane men must show courage and defined righteousness as straightening finances and language so people cannot easily turn criminal.

sentences.zh: 高帝受命，制約令，定法律，傳之後世，可常施行。

translations.literal: The Supreme Founder received the mandate, made compact orders, fixed statutes and laws, transmitted them to later generations—they could be constantly applied.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu founded the Han with concise ordinances and enduring codes that later reigns were meant to live by.

sentences.zh: 文帝寬惠溫克，遭世康平，因時施恩，省去肉刑，除相坐之法，他皆率由舊章，天下幾致升平。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was broad, kind, warm, and restrained; encountering an age healthy and peaceful, according with the times he spread grace, omitted mutilating punishments, removed mutual-liability law; all else followed old chapters—the realm nearly reached rising peace.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen ruled gently in prosperous times, commuting corporal punishments and abolishing guilt-by-association while leaving the rest of Gaozu's code intact, bringing the realm within sight of perfect calm.

sentences.zh: 武帝值中國隆盛，財力有餘，出兵命將，征伐遠方，軍役數興，百姓罷弊，豪傑犯禁，奸吏弄法，故設遁匿之科，著知縱之律。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu encountered Central States flourishing and wealth strength abundant; he raised armies and ordered generals, punished expeditions to distant regions; military service arose repeatedly; the hundred surnames were exhausted; heroes violated prohibitions; crafty clerks toyed with law—therefore he established statutes on flight and concealment, promulgated laws on knowing release.
translations.idiomatic: Wudi mobilized endless campaigns while the treasury still looked full; commoners broke under corvée, bold men flouted bans, and clerks twisted verdicts, so the throne added clauses against fugitives and judges who knowingly went lenient.

sentences.zh: 宣帝聰明正直，履道握要，以禦海內，臣下奉憲，不失繩墨。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuandi was intelligent, wise, upright, and straight; treading the Way and grasping essentials, he used them to govern within the seas; subordinates observed statutes, did not miss inked lines.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan combined clarity with integrity, held to fundamentals, and kept officials snapping their rulings to the straight ink-line.

sentences.zh: 元帝法律，少所改更，天下稱安。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan's laws and statutes had little alteration; the realm called it peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: Yuandi tinkered little with the code and the realm still pronounced itself secure.

sentences.zh: 孝成、孝哀，承平繼體，即位日淺，聽斷尚寡。

translations.literal: Emperors Cheng and Ai inherited peace and succeeded the body; the days since ascending were shallow; hearings and judgments were still few.
translations.idiomatic: Chenodi and Aidi inherited a tranquil throne and had ruled only briefly, so they heard few capital cases themselves.

sentences.zh: 丞相王嘉等猥以數年之間，虧除先帝舊約，穿令斷律，凡百餘事，或不便於政，或不厭人心。

translations.literal: Chancellor Wang Jia and others rashly in the space of several years injured and removed former emperors' old compacts, bored through orders and broke statutes—totalling over a hundred matters—some inconvenient to government, some unsatisfying to people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years Chancellor Wang Jia's faction punched loopholes through edicts and statutes—more than a hundred changes—that often harmed governance or offended public sentiment.

sentences.zh: 臣謹表取其尤妨政事、害善良者，傅奏如左。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully lists those that especially obstruct government affairs and harm the good and kind, transmitting the memorial as at left.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore excerpt the worst offenses against policy and decency and attach them herewith.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下苞五常，履九德，推時撥亂，博施濟時，而反因循季世末節，衰微軌跡，誠非所以還初反本，據元更始也。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty embraces the five constants, treads the nine powers, pushes the age and removes chaos, broadly bestows and aids the age—yet on the contrary follows late-age marginal tracks, declining faint footprints—this is truly not the means to return to the beginning and reverse to the root, to seize the origin and renew the start.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty embodies the cardinal virtues and rescues the age, yet clinging to dying expedients from the late Han hardly restores founding clarity or lets you reset the mandate.

sentences.zh: 願陛下宣詔有司，悉舉初元、建平之所穿鑿，考其輕重，察其化俗，足以知政教所處，擇其善者而從之，其不善者而改之，定不易之典，施之無窮，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty proclaim to the offices responsible, entirely raise what Chuyuan and Jianping bored through and carved, examine their light and heavy, observe how they transformed custom—sufficient to know where government and teaching stand—choose the good among them and follow it; among the not good change it; fix unchanging canons; apply them without end—the realm will be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Please order the ministries to audit every Jianping-era loophole, weigh each reform's costs and moral effect, keep what still serves civilization and repeal what corrupts it, then engrave a stable code that future reigns never need rewrite—the empire will owe you a debt of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 至章帝時，尚書陳寵上疏曰：「先王之政，賞不僭，刑不濫，與其不得已，寧僭不濫。

translations.literal: When it reached Emperor Zhang's time, Minister Chen Chong submitted a memorial saying: "The government of former kings did not overstep in rewards, did not overflow in punishments; compared with being forced to choose, better overstep than overflow."
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhang, Chen Chong argued that sage kings never mismatched rewards or punishments and that, if forced to err, excess mercy beats careless cruelty.

sentences.zh: 故唐堯著典曰'流宥五刑，眚災肆赦'。

translations.literal: Therefore Tang Yao wrote in the canon: 'Commute and forgive the five punishments; accidental calamities receive generous pardon.'
translations.idiomatic: The canon Yao left pairs commuting sentences with mercy for innocent disaster.

sentences.zh: 帝舜命皋陶以'五宅三居，惟明克允'。

translations.literal: Emperor Shun commanded Gao Yao with 'five dwellings, three residences—only clarity can achieve trust.'
translations.idiomatic: Shun instructed Gao Yao to grade exile by three regional zones and judge only with luminous fairness.

sentences.zh: 文王重《易》六爻，而列叢棘之聽；

translations.literal: King Wen doubled the six lines of the Changes, and arrayed listening amid thorn-brush;
translations.idiomatic: King Wen deepened the hexagrams and still heard capital appeals inside a ring of spiny stakes.

sentences.zh: 周公作《立政》，戒成王勿誤乎庶獄。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou made "Established Government," warning King Cheng not to err in the multitude of prisons.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou's "Established Government" warns a young king never to bungle criminal appeals.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位，率由此義，而有司執事，未悉奉承。

translations.literal: Your Majesty upon ascending the throne generally followed this meaning, yet those who hold office in departments have not entirely received and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: You began your reign pledging this humane standard, yet many handlers downstairs still ignore it.

sentences.zh: 斷獄者急於榜格酷烈之痛，執憲者繁於詐欺放濫之文，違本離實，棰楚為奸，或因公行私，以逞威福。

translations.literal: Those who decide prisons hurry toward the pain of cudgel norms fierce and cruel; those who uphold statutes are tangled in writings of deceit, looseness, and overflow—violating root and departing from substance; beatings become crafty; some borrow public duty to pursue private ends, thereby displaying might and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Judges rush to rack and whip while clerks bury truth in jargon; torture invites corruption and petty tyrants abuse delegated power.

sentences.zh: 夫為政也，猶張琴瑟，大弦急者小弦絕，故子貢非臧孫之猛法，而美鄭僑之仁政。

translations.literal: Governing is like tuning zither and se: when the great string is urgent the small strings break—therefore Zigong condemned Zangsun's fierce laws and praised Zichan of Zheng's benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: Policy works like a lute: wrench the bass too tight and higher strings snap—which is why Zigong scorned cruel Lu jurists but praised the humane reforms of Zichan in Zheng.

sentences.zh: 方今聖德充塞，假於上下，宜因此時，隆先聖之務，蕩滌煩苛，輕薄棰楚，以濟群生，廣至德也。

translations.literal: Now sagely virtue fills and reaches above and below; it is fitting to take advantage of this time, elevate the tasks of former sages, wash away fussy harshness, lighten and thin beatings and rods, thereby aiding the multitude of lives, extending utmost virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred virtue already saturates court and countryside—use this moment to revive antique mercy, strip statutes of petty cruelty, ease beatings, relieve common folk, and widen your humane prestige.

sentences.zh: 」帝納寵言，決罪行刑，務于寬厚。

translations.literal: " The emperor adopted Chong's words; deciding crimes and applying punishments, he strove for leniency and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Zhang accepted Chen Chong's plea and tilted every verdict toward mercy.

sentences.zh: 其後遂詔有司，禁絕鑽钅贊諸酷痛舊制，解祅惡之禁，除文致之請，讞五十餘事，定著於令。

translations.literal: Afterward he then ordered the offices responsible to forbid and cut off branding irons, piercing drills, and various cruel painful old systems; to loosen prohibitions on malign omens; to remove pleadings of twisting prose; for over fifty matters of final review, to fix and record in orders.
translations.idiomatic: He soon banned iron branding, pierce-screws, and other torments enshrined in old practice, dropped prosecutions for fabricated occult charges, ended malicious readings of the code, and codified more than fifty appellate clarifications.

sentences.zh: 是後獄法和平。

translations.literal: After this prison law was peaceful and harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Criminal procedure thereafter turned calm and even-handed.

sentences.zh: 永元六年，寵又代郭躬為廷尉，復校律令，刑法溢于《甫刑》者，奏除之，曰：「臣聞禮經三百，威儀三千，故《甫刑》大辟二百，五刑之屬三千。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongyuan, Chong again replaced Guo Gong as commandant of justice, again collated statutes and orders—those punishments and laws that overflowed beyond the Fu punishments, memorialized to remove them, saying: "Your servant has heard ritual classics number three hundred, awe-inspiring deportments three thousand; therefore the Fu punishments had two hundred capital crimes; categories of the five punishments three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan 6 Chen Chong succeeded Guo Gong at the Ministry of Justice, reviewed the entire corpus, and petitioned to strike clauses exceeding even the Mu-era Fu canon: "Ritual preserves three hundred anchors and three thousand gestures of deportment, matching the Fu code's two hundred capital crimes among three thousand punishments.

sentences.zh: 禮之所去，刑之所取，失禮即入刑，相為表裏者也。

translations.literal: What ritual removes, punishment takes; missing ritual then enters punishment—they are mutual outer and inner.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment picks up every obligation ritual lets fall—law and rite are two sides of one coat.

sentences.zh: 今律令，犯罪應死刑者六百一十，耐罪千六百九十八，贖罪以下二千六百八十一，溢于《甫刑》千九百八十九，其四百一十大辟，千五百耐罪，七十九贖罪。

translations.literal: Now in statutes and orders, crimes answering to death penalty number six hundred ten; shave-hair crimes one thousand six hundred ninety-eight; redeemable crimes and below two thousand six hundred eighty-one; overflowing beyond the Fu punishments one thousand nine hundred eighty-nine—among them four hundred ten capital crimes, one thousand five hundred shave-hair crimes, seventy-nine redeemable crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Current Han codes list 610 capital offenses, 1,698 mutilating sentences, and 2,681 redeemable offenses—1,989 clauses beyond what the Fu canon contemplated, including 410 capital counts, 1,500 hair-shaving penalties, and 79 redeemable articles.

sentences.zh: 《春秋保乾圖》曰：'王者三百年一蠲法。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Baogan Diagram says: 'Kings once every three hundred years waive the laws.
translations.idiomatic: The apocryphal Baogan Diagram teaches that kings should overhaul statutes roughly once every three centuries.

sentences.zh: '漢興以來，三百二年，憲令稍增，科條無限。

translations.literal: ' Since Han's rise, three hundred two years—foundational orders have gradually increased; statutory clauses are without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Han has now ruled 302 years; orders swell steadily while clauses multiply without ceiling.

sentences.zh: 又律有三家，說各駁異。

translations.literal: Moreover the statutes have three houses; explanations each contradict and differ.
translations.idiomatic: Three rival schools interpret the code, and their readings contradict one another.

sentences.zh: 刑法繁多，宜令三公、廷尉集平律令，應經合義可施行者，大辟二百，耐罪、贖罪二千八百，合為三千，與禮相應。

translations.literal: Punishments and laws are numerous and excessive; it is fitting to order the Three Dukes and commandant of justice to gather and harmonize statutes and orders—those matching classics and joining righteousness that can be applied: capital two hundred; shave-hair and redeemable crimes two thousand eight hundred—totaling three thousand, corresponding with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Three Excellencies and the Ministry of Justice reconcile Han law with the canon: retain two hundred capital statutes plus twenty-eight hundred lesser offenses—three thousand clauses mirroring ritual's triads—and discard the surplus.

sentences.zh: 其餘千九百八十九事，悉可詳除。

translations.literal: The remaining one thousand nine hundred eighty-nine matters can all be examined and removed.
translations.idiomatic: The other 1,989 provisions deserve systematic repeal.

sentences.zh: 使百姓改易視聽，以成大化，致刑措之美，傳之無窮。

translations.literal: Cause the hundred surnames to change hearing and sight, thereby achieve great transformation, bring about the beauty of punishments set aside, transmit it without end.
translations.idiomatic: Refashion what ordinary families hear and see, complete moral transformation, approach the age when punishments lie unused, and hand that achievement down forever.

sentences.zh: 」未及施行，會寵抵罪，遂寢。

translations.literal: " Before it reached implementation, Chong encountered guilt for an offense, then it was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial stalled before promulgation because Chen Chong himself faced indictment.

sentences.zh: 寵子忠。

translations.literal: Chong's son Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chen Zhong figures next.

sentences.zh: 忠後復為尚書，略依寵意，奏上三十三條，為《決事比》，以省請讞之弊。

translations.literal: Zhong afterward again became minister; broadly following Chong's intent, he memorialized thirty-three articles, making "Decided Cases as Precedents," thereby saving the harm of requests for final review.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhong later rose again within the Ministry, distilled his father's ideas into thirty-three binding precedents collected as the Decided Cases as Precedents, and closed loopholes that clogged appellate paperwork.

sentences.zh: 又上除蠶室刑，解贓吏三世禁錮，狂易殺人得減重論，母子兄弟相代死聽赦所代者，事皆施行。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to remove silkworm-room punishment; to loosen corrupt clerks' three-generation prohibition and binding; that insane persons who kill may receive reduced heavy judgment; that mothers and sons and brothers substituting death for one another listen to pardon for the one substituted—all matters were implemented.
translations.idiomatic: His supplements abolished castration workshops, lifted perpetual disqualification on embezzlers' descendants, allowed lighter sentences for insane killers, and permitted relatives who swapped places on the scaffold to receive the intended pardon—all enacted.

sentences.zh: 雖時有蠲革，而舊律繁蕪，未經纂集。

translations.literal: Although there were timely removals and reforms, old statutes were numerous and tangled, not yet compiled and gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Piecemeal repeals helped, yet the Eastern Han code stayed overgrown because nobody produced a unified digest.

sentences.zh: 獻帝建安元年，應劭又刪定律令，以為《漢議》，表奏之曰：「夫國之大事，莫尚載籍。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xian's first year of Jian'an, Ying Shao again edited and fixed statutes and orders, making them "Han Deliberations," memorializing them with the statement: "Of the state's great matters, none exalts records above.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 1 Ying Shao pruned the statutes into his Han Deliberations and prefaced the memorial: "No state duty outweighs preserving written law.

sentences.zh: 載籍也者，決嫌疑，明是非，賞刑之宜，允執厥中，俾後之人永有鑒焉。

translations.literal: Records are those that resolve doubt and suspicion, clarify right and wrong, the propriety of reward and punishment, sincerely hold their center—thereby causing later people forever to have a mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Archives settle doubts, separate right from wrong, balance reward and punishment, and hand posterity a lasting mirror.

sentences.zh: 故膠東相董仲舒老病致仕，朝廷每有政議，數遣廷尉張湯親至陋巷，問其得失，於是作《春秋折獄》二百三十二事，動以《經》對，言之詳矣。

translations.literal: Therefore Chancellor of Jiaodong Dong Zhongshu, old and ill, retired; whenever the court had policy deliberations, repeatedly they sent Commandant of Justice Zhang Tang in person to humble alleys, asking his gains and losses; thereupon he made "Spring and Autumn Judging Prison Cases" two hundred thirty-two matters, always answering with the Classics—his words were detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Retired counselor Dong Zhongshu still advised Zhang Tang on classical jurisprudence, yielding 232 Spring and Autumn case rulings grounded in canonical debate.

sentences.zh: 逆臣董卓，蕩覆王室，典憲焚燎，靡有孑遺，開闢以來，莫或茲酷。

translations.literal: The rebellious minister Dong Zhuo overturned the royal house; canons and statutes were burned—none had surviving remnant; since the opening of creation, none perhaps has been this cruel.
translations.idiomatic: The traitor Dong Zhuo torched legal archives along with the capital—perhaps no catastrophe since creation erased institutions so utterly.

sentences.zh: 今大駕東邁，巡省許都，拔出險難，其命惟新。

translations.literal: Now the grand chariot moves east, touring and inspecting Xudu, pulling out from peril and hardship—its mandate is only renewal.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial train now advances east to Xu, escaping catastrophe and refounding the mandate.

sentences.zh: 臣竊不自揆，輒撰具《律本章句》、《尚書舊事》、《廷尉板令》、《決事比例》、《司徒都目》、《五曹詔書》及《春秋折獄》，凡二百五十篇，蠲去復重，為之節文。

translations.literal: Your servant privately does not measure himself, rashly compiled and completed "Statute Original Chapter and Sentences," "Old Affairs of the Document," "Commandant of Justice Plank Orders," "Decided Cases and Ratios," "Minister of Education Capital Catalogue," "Five Bureau Edicts," and "Spring and Autumn Judging Prison Cases"—in all two hundred fifty pieces; removed duplicates and repetitions; for them made condensed text.
translations.idiomatic: Without waiting for permission I collated 250 chapters drawn from statutory glosses, palace precedents, ministry placards, ratios, board catalogs, edicts, and Spring and Autumn precedents, pruning overlap into concise articles.

sentences.zh: 又集《議駁》三十篇，以類相從，凡八十二事。

translations.literal: Also gathered "Deliberation Refutations" thirty pieces, following category together—in all eighty-two matters.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty more volumes titled Deliberation Refutations sort eighty-two contested issues by topic.

sentences.zh: 其見《漢書》二十五，《漢記》四，皆刪敘潤色，以全本體。

translations.literal: Those items appearing in the Han Documents number twenty-five, and in the Han Records four—all were edited, arranged, and polished to preserve the complete corpus.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-five entries drawn from the Han Documents and four from the Han Records were trimmed and polished so the compilation stays internally consistent.

sentences.zh: 其二十六，博采古今瑰瑋之士，德義可觀。

translations.literal: Item twenty-six broadly gathers splendid scholars ancient and modern whose virtue and righteousness repay inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Section twenty-six collects noteworthy voices past and present whose moral insight still instructs.

sentences.zh: 其二十七，臣所創造。

translations.literal: Item twenty-seven your servant personally composed.
translations.idiomatic: Section twenty-seven records material I authored myself.

sentences.zh: 《左氏》云：'雖有姬薑，不棄憔悴；

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary says: 'Though there are fine silks from Ji and Jiang, one does not discard the worn and tired;
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Tradition remarks that even when fine Qi and Jiang silks lie ready, one still keeps threadbare cloth.

sentences.zh: 雖有絲麻，不棄菅蒯。

translations.literal: Though there are silk and hemp, one does not discard rush and wicker.'
translations.idiomatic: Even with silk and hemp at hand, humble rush cord still has its place.

sentences.zh: '蓋所以代匱也。

translations.literal: ' That is how shortages are supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Those humble materials fill whatever the treasury lacks.

sentences.zh: 是用敢露頑才，廁於明哲之末，雖未足綱紀國體，宣洽時雍。

translations.literal: Therefore I dare expose my stubborn talent and place it at the tail of the wise and enlightened—though it is insufficient to order the national body or spread the harmony of the age.
translations.idiomatic: So I risk adding my crude scholarship after your luminaries—far short of codifying the body politic or proclaiming universal peace.

sentences.zh: 庶幾觀察，增闡聖德。

translations.literal: Perhaps upon inspection it may expand and clarify sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet perhaps cursory review will still enlarge readers' sense of your virtue.

sentences.zh: 惟因萬機之餘暇，遊意省覽。

translations.literal: Only in the leisure remaining from myriad threads of state, let your mind roam in reading.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever ten thousand state affairs leave a spare hour, let these pages reward a leisurely glance.

sentences.zh: 」獻帝善之，於是舊事存焉。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xian praised it, and the old materials were thereby preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xian endorsed the collection, and those precedents survived.

sentences.zh: 是時天下將亂，百姓有土崩之勢，刑罰不足以懲惡，於是名儒大才故遼東太守崔實、大司農鄭玄、大鴻臚陳紀之徒，咸以為宜復行肉刑。

translations.literal: At that time the realm verged on chaos; the common people showed a landslide momentum; punishments could not suffice to punish evil—therefore great Confucian talents such as former Liaodong Governor Cui Shi, Grand Minister of Agriculture Zheng Xuan, and Grand Herald Chen Ji all held that corporal punishment ought to be restored.
translations.idiomatic: As order collapsed and punishments lost deterrent force, luminaries such as ex-Liaodong governor Cui Shi, minister Zheng Xuan, and herald Chen Ji urged restoring mutilating penalties.

sentences.zh: 漢朝既不議其事，故無所用矣。

translations.literal: The Han court never debated the matter, so nothing came of it.
translations.idiomatic: Because the court took no decision, the proposal died quietly.

sentences.zh: 及魏武帝匡輔漢室，尚書令荀彧博訪百官，復欲申之，而少府孔融議以為：「古者敦厖，善否區別，吏端刑清政簡，一無過失，百姓有罪，皆自取之。

translations.literal: When King Wu of Wei aided the Han house, Director of the Secretariat Xun Yu consulted broadly among the hundred officials and wished to advance the proposal again, but Privy Treasurer Kong Rong argued, saying, "In high antiquity they were simple and vast; good and evil were distinct; clerks were upright, punishments were clear, government was simple, and in all there were no errors; when the common people had guilt they all brought it on themselves."
translations.idiomatic: After Cao Cao shored up the Han, Xun Yu polled the bureaucracy to revive corporal punishment, but Kong Rong began his rebuttal: antiquity was plain and transparent; law ran clean; any fault lay with the people themselves.

sentences.zh: 末世陵遲，風化壞亂，政撓其俗，法害其教。

translations.literal: In declining ages slopes slip; customs spoil and disorder; government bends custom; law injures teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Later eras decay: morale frays, institutions warp until policy twists customs and statutes sabotage moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 故曰'上失其道，人散久矣'。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said 'When those above lose their Way, the people scatter—long ago.'
translations.idiomatic: Hence the adage that once rulers abandon the Way, their subjects drift beyond recall.

sentences.zh: 而欲繩之以古刑，投之以殘棄，非所謂與時消息也。

translations.literal: Yet wishing to tie them to ancient mutilation and cast them away as wreckage is not what is called ebbing and flowing with the age.
translations.idiomatic: Slapping archaic mutilations onto modern offenders ignores how institutions must breathe with their times.

sentences.zh: 紂斮朝涉之脛，天下謂為無道。

translations.literal: Zhou cut the shin of a man wading the ford at dawn—the realm called him devoid of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhou's pointless shin-cutting frolic branded him irredeemably cruel.

sentences.zh: 夫九牧之地，千八百君，若各刖一人，是天下常有千八百紂也，求世休和，弗可得已。

translations.literal: Across the Nine Pastures' lands were eighteen hundred lords; if each severed one foot, the realm would forever harbor eighteen hundred Zhous—seeking universal peace cannot be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen hundred feudal lords times one amputation each still yields eighteen hundred tyrants—never harmony.

sentences.zh: 且被刑之人，慮不念生，志在思死，類多趨惡，莫復歸正。

translations.literal: Moreover those who have suffered mutilation do not plan on living; their hearts dwell on death; most incline toward evil and never return to rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: The branded stop investing in survival; hope dies, recidivism rises, rehabilitation falters.

sentences.zh: 夙沙亂齊，伊戾禍宋，趙高、英布，為世大患。

translations.literal: Su Sha threw Qi into chaos; Yi Li harmed Song; Zhao Gao and Ying Bu became great scourges to the age.
translations.idiomatic: History lists Su Sha, Yi Li, Zhao Gao, and Ying Bu among disasters spawned by society's outcasts.

sentences.zh: 不能止人遂為非也，適足絕人還為善耳。

translations.literal: They cannot stop others from thus doing wrong—they only suffice to cut people off from returning to good.
translations.idiomatic: Corporal shame does not deter crime; it simply bars redemption.

sentences.zh: 雖忠如鬻拳，信如卞和，智如孫臏，冤如巷伯，才如史遷，達如子政，一罹刀鋸，沒世不齒。

translations.literal: Though loyal like Yu Quan, trustworthy like Bian He, wise like Sun Bin, wronged like the Lane Uncle, talented like Sima Qian, penetrating like Liu Xiang—once they meet knife and saw, they are spurned forever.
translations.idiomatic: Men as upright as Yu Quan or brilliant as Sima Qian become permanent pariahs after mutilation.

sentences.zh: 是太甲之思庸，穆公之霸秦，陳湯之都賴，魏尚之臨邊，無所復施也。

translations.literal: Therefore Taijia's reflection on the common man, Duke Mu's hegemony of Qin, Chen Tang's merit at Lai, Wei Shang's guarding the frontier—none could again be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Second chances like Taijia's reform or Wei Shang's generalship vanish once the law brands a body ruined.

sentences.zh: 漢開改惡之路，凡為此也。

translations.literal: Han opened a path to reform the wicked—generally for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Han deliberately created alternatives to mutilation for exactly these humane reasons.

sentences.zh: 故明德之君，遠度深惟，棄短就長，不苟革其政者也。

translations.literal: Therefore a ruler of bright virtue, measuring far and pondering deep, discards the short-term and embraces the long-term, and does not rashly alter his institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Wise sovereigns weigh distant consequences and refuse cosmetic cruelty.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷善之，卒不改焉。

translations.literal: " The court praised Kong Rong's view and ultimately made no change.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberative assembly sided with Kong Rong and dropped the proposal.

sentences.zh: 及魏國建，陳紀子群時為御史中丞，魏武帝下令又欲復之，使群申其父論。

translations.literal: When the Wei state was founded, Chen Qun—Chen Ji's son—was censor-in-chief; King Wu of Wei issued edicts reviving the debate and ordered Chen Qun to restate his father's argument.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei stood as a kingdom, Chen Qun inherited his father's portfolio and had to defend corporal punishment anew.

sentences.zh: 群深陳其便。

translations.literal: Chen Qun elaborated at length its convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qun laid out pragmatic gains in exhaustive detail.

sentences.zh: 時鐘繇為相國，亦贊成之，而奉常王脩不同其議。

translations.literal: At the time Zhong Yao served as chancellor and endorsed the plan, but libationer Wang Xiu disputed it.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhong Yao concurred, yet Minister Wang Xiu held firm opposition.

sentences.zh: 魏武帝亦難以籓國改漢朝之制，遂寢不行。

translations.literal: King Wu of Wei also hesitated to let a vassal regime overturn Han precedent, so the matter lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao shrank from rewriting Han law from a subordinate court and shelved the initiative.

sentences.zh: 於是乃定甲子科，犯釱左右趾者易以木械，是時乏鐵，故易以木焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Jiazi code fixed matters: offenders shackled on both feet wore wooden cangues instead—iron was scarce, hence wood.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiazi reform swapped iron fetters for timber stocks because metal ran short.

sentences.zh: 又嫌漢律太重，故令依律論者聽得科半，使從半減也。

translations.literal: Because Han statutes felt excessively harsh, orders allowed judges applying statutes to take half an article, securing an automatic half reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Deeming Han penalties cruel, Wei permitted sentencing at half the nominal statutory grade.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝受禪，又議肉刑。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Wei accepted abdication, ministers debated corporal punishment once more.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Pi's accession reopened the corporal-punishment controversy.

sentences.zh: 詳議未定，會有軍事，復寢。

translations.literal: Detailed deliberation never settled before campaigns intervened, so the issue stalled again.
translations.idiomatic: War interrupted the conference and the reform slept.

sentences.zh: 時有大女劉硃，撾子婦酷暴，前後三婦自殺，論硃減死輸作尚方，因是下怨毒殺人減死之令。

translations.literal: An elderly woman, Liu Zhu, brutalized her daughters-in-law until three successive wives killed themselves; Zhu received commuted death labor in the Court Artisans, prompting an edict reducing sentences for killings driven by bitter grievance.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhu drove three daughters-in-law to suicide, judges spared her life for hard labor—lawmakers then generalized mercy for passionate homicides.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝改士庶罰金之令，男聽以罰金，婦人加笞還從鞭督之例，以其形體裸露故也。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming revised fines for nobles and commoners: men might redeem with cash; women faced extra flogging under whipping rules because exposing female bodies was deemed improper.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Mingdi let gentlemen buy off fines while ordering female offenders flogged instead of stripped for cash penalties.

sentences.zh: 是時承用秦漢舊律，其文起自魏文侯師李悝。

translations.literal: Officials still enforced Qin-Han statutes whose lineage began with Li Kui, tutor to Marquis Wen of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Wei jurists continued Han codes rooted in Li Kui's Warring States canon.

sentences.zh: 悝撰次諸國法，著《法經》。

translations.literal: Li Kui arranged the laws of each state and composed the Classic of Law.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui codified interstate precedents into the Classic of Law.

sentences.zh: 以為王者之政，莫急於盜賊，故其律始于《盜賊》。

translations.literal: He argued that banditry tops a king's worries, so his code opens with Robbery and Banditry.
translations.idiomatic: Because predators threaten stability most, his text leads with theft and violence.

sentences.zh: 盜賊須劾捕，故著《網捕》二篇。

translations.literal: Bandits require impeachment and arrest, hence he added the paired chapters Nets and Arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Suppression chapters followed immediately for pursuit and capture.

sentences.zh: 其輕狡、越城、博戲、借假不廉、淫侈逾制以為《雜律》一篇，又以《具律》具其加減。

translations.literal: Light fraud, wall jumping, gambling, bogus loans, graft, and extravagance beyond sumptuary rules became one Miscellaneous chapter; the Completing chapter handled sentencing offsets.
translations.idiomatic: Petty vice and administrative drift filled a Miscellaneous fascicle while the Completing statute calibrated aggravation and mitigation.

sentences.zh: 是故所著六篇而已，然皆罪名之制也。

translations.literal: Thus only six fascicles exist, yet each prescribes offense labels.
translations.idiomatic: Six slim volumes nonetheless enumerated every named crime.

sentences.zh: 商君受之以相秦。

translations.literal: Lord Shang inherited the package and served Qin as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Yang imported Li Kui's skeleton into Qin's centralized reform.

sentences.zh: 漢承秦制，蕭何定律，除參夷連坐之罪，增部主見知之條，益事律《興》、《廄》、《戶》三篇，合為九篇。

translations.literal: Han adopted Qin's skeleton; Xiao He refined it—stripping kin-extinction and collective guilt, adding departmental-liability clauses, and expanding business law with Rise, Stables, and Household fascicles for nine total.
translations.idiomatic: Han fused Qin severity with Xiao He's softer overlay—nine core codes replacing collective punishment with departmental oversight chapters.

sentences.zh: 叔孫通益律所不及，傍章十八篇。

translations.literal: Shusun Tong patched gaps with eighteen supplementary ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Shusun Tong appended eighteen ceremonial side statutes.

sentences.zh: 張湯《越宮律》二十七篇。

translations.literal: Zhang Tang contributed twenty-seven Palace-Crossing statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tang added twenty-seven palace-security provisions.

sentences.zh: 趙禹《朝律》六篇。

translations.literal: Zhao Yu contributed six Court statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yu supplied six audience protocols.

sentences.zh: 合六十篇。

translations.literal: Sixty fascicles altogether.
translations.idiomatic: The Han archive thus stacked sixty statutory bundles.

sentences.zh: 又漢時決事，集為《令甲》以下三百餘篇，及司徒鮑公撰嫁娶辭訟決為《法比都目》，凡九百六卷。

translations.literal: Han verdict digests yielded three hundred further fascicles after Decree A, while Minister Bao cataloged marriage suits into the Comparative Index—960 scrolls total.
translations.idiomatic: Case law ballooned: three hundred decree codices plus Bao Xun's 960-scroll marriage register.

sentences.zh: 世有增損，率皆集類為篇，結事為章。

translations.literal: Each generation added or trimmed, generally grouping topics into fascicles and clustering incidents into chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Every reign reshuffled clauses into thematic fascicles and episodic chapters.

sentences.zh: 一章之中或事過數十，事類雖同，輕重乖異。

translations.literal: Within a single chapter dozens of fact patterns may appear; though the class matches, severity diverges.
translations.idiomatic: Single chapters now mixed dozens of fact patterns of wildly different weight.

sentences.zh: 而通條連句，上下相蒙，雖大體異篇，實相采入。

translations.literal: Connected clauses and nested sentences shroud one another; though different fascicles, content cross-cites.
translations.idiomatic: Cross-references tangled: separate books silently imported one another's clauses.

sentences.zh: 《盜律》有賊傷之例，《賊律》有盜章之文，《興律》有上獄之法，《廄律》有逮捕之事，若此之比，錯糅無常。

translations.literal: Robbery statutes carried wound provisions; bandit statutes duplicated robbery language; rise statutes embedded jail procedures; stables statutes tucked arrest powers—such overlaps knew no pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Theft law mingled with assault law; stable regulations housed arrest rules—definitions blurred beyond navigation.

sentences.zh: 後人生意，各為章句。

translations.literal: Later jurists spun private glosses on each clause.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators multiplied rival readings atop every line.

sentences.zh: 叔孫宣、郭令卿、馬融、鄭玄諸儒章句十有餘家，家數十萬言。

translations.literal: Shusun Xuan, Guo Lingqing, Ma Rong, Zheng Xuan—more than ten exegetical schools—each counting hundreds of thousands of characters.
translations.idiomatic: Ten-plus scholarly houses produced hundreds of thousands of commentary characters apiece.

sentences.zh: 凡斷罪所當由用者，合二萬六千二百七十二條，七百七十三萬二千二百餘言，言數益繁，覽者益難。

translations.literal: Applicable sentencing combinations reached 26,272 clauses totaling more than 7.73 million characters—the prose snowballed while comprehension collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Effective sentencing drew on 26,272 article intersections spanning 7.73 million characters—unreadable sprawl.

sentences.zh: 天子於是下詔，但用鄭氏章句，不得雜用餘家。

translations.literal: The emperor mandated exclusive reliance on Zheng Xuan's gloss—no mixing rival schools.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial fiat canonized Zheng Xuan and banned eclectic citation.

sentences.zh: 衛覬又奏曰：「刑法者，國家之所貴重，而私議之所輕賤；

translations.literal: Wei Ji memorialized: criminal law is what the state treasures yet gossip trivializes;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ji warned that statutes deserve reverence even when chatter treats them lightly;

sentences.zh: 獄吏者，百姓之所懸命，而選用者之所卑下。

translations.literal: prison clerks hold commoners' lives yet appointments despise them.
translations.idiomatic: jailors anchor people's survival yet the service ranks rock bottom.

sentences.zh: 王政之弊，未必不由此也。

translations.literal: The maladies of royal government—perhaps they begin right there.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial government rots when law becomes a low-status afterthought.

sentences.zh: 請置律博士，轉相教授。

translations.literal: He asked to found chairs of legal erudition and rotate instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed state-sponsored law professors to train the bench.

sentences.zh: 」事遂施行。

translations.literal: " The court adopted the idea.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved and created the post.

sentences.zh: 然而律文煩廣，事比眾多，離本依末，決獄之吏如廷尉獄吏范洪受囚絹二丈，附輕法論之，獄吏劉象受屬偏考囚張茂物故，附重法論之。

translations.literal: Still, statute verbiage swelled, analogies proliferated, and judges abandoned principle for edge cases—like commandant clerk Fan Hong who took two bolts of inmate silk and applied the lightest clause, or clerk Liu Xiang who bowed to a bribe, coerced defendant Zhang Mao to death, and applied the harshest clause.
translations.idiomatic: Yet prolix codes invited manipulation: Fan Hong pocketed silk and chose lenient readings while Liu Xiang took bribes, tortured Zhang Mao to death, and chose cruelty.

sentences.zh: 洪、象雖皆棄市，而輕枉者相繼。

translations.literal: Although both Fan and Liu were executed in the marketplace, wrongful lenity continued without end.
translations.idiomatic: Marketplace executions did not stop softer miscarriages from stacking up.

sentences.zh: 是時太傅鐘繇又上疏求復肉刑，詔下其奏，司徒王朗議又不同。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Zhong Yao again urged restoring corporal punishment; the edict forwarded his paper, but Minister Wang Lang dissented.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yao revived the corporal-punishment plea; Wang Lang answered with another firm refusal.

sentences.zh: 時議者百餘人，與朗同者多。

translations.literal: More than a hundred officials debated; most followed Wang Lang.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred voices debated, most siding with Wang Lang.

sentences.zh: 帝以吳蜀未平，又寢。

translations.literal: The emperor, with Wu and Shu still unbeaten, shelved the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: War with Shu and Wu kept the emperor from reopening the wound.

sentences.zh: 其後，天子又下詔改定刑制，命司空陳群、散騎常侍劉邵、給事黃門侍郎韓遜、議郎庾嶷、中郎黃休、荀詵等刪約舊科，傍采漢律，定為魏法，制《新律》十八篇，《州郡令》四十五篇，《尚書官令》、《軍中令》，合百八十餘篇。

translations.literal: Later an edict commanded Chen Qun, Liu Shao, Han Xun, Yu Yi, Huang Xiu, Xun Shen, and others to condense old statutes, borrow Han clauses, and forge Wei law: eighteen New Statutes, forty-five Prefecture Decrees, Secretariat and Army Camp decrees—over 180 fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Wei ordered Chen Qun, Liu Shao, Han Xun, Yu Yi, Huang Xiu, and Xun Shen to forge the New Code—eighteen core statutes plus prefectural and military decrees exceeding 180 fascicles.

sentences.zh: 其序略曰：

translations.literal: Its preface reads in outline:
translations.idiomatic: Their preface opens:

sentences.zh: 舊律所難知者，由於六篇篇少故也。

translations.literal: Old statutes felt opaque because six foundational chapters were too few.
translations.idiomatic: Sparse chapter counts left early Han codes skeletal.

sentences.zh: 篇少則文荒，文荒則事寡，事寡則罪漏。

translations.literal: Few chapters meant bare text; bare text meant thin coverage; thin coverage meant offenses slipped through.
translations.idiomatic: Thin skeletons leaked crimes faster than editors patched them.

sentences.zh: 是以後人稍增，更與本體相離。

translations.literal: Later jurists kept stapling addenda until texts drifted from their roots.
translations.idiomatic: Successive glossators drifted ever farther from Li Kui's core.

sentences.zh: 今制新律，宜都總事類，多其篇條。

translations.literal: Drafting fresh statutes therefore demands fuller topical sorting and richer fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Rewriting Wei law meant clustering topics into denser fascicles.

sentences.zh: 舊律因秦《法經》，就增三篇，而《具律》不移，因在第六。

translations.literal: Han codes inherited Qin's Classic of Law, added three fascicles, yet left the Completing statute stranded mid-code as fascicle six.
translations.idiomatic: Han pasted three new books onto Qin's six yet stranded sentencing offsets awkwardly in sixth place.

sentences.zh: 罪條例既不在始，又不在終，非篇章之義。

translations.literal: Sentencing rules belong neither at the start nor the finish—contrary to sound chapter design.
translations.idiomatic: General sentencing rules sitting mid-volume violated drafting logic.

sentences.zh: 故集罪例以為《刑名》，冠於律首。

translations.literal: Editors therefore gathered offense paradigms into a Punishment Names fascicle crowning the corpus.
translations.idiomatic: Wei compilers extracted definitions into a Punishment Names preface atop the code.

sentences.zh: 《盜律》有劫略、恐猲、和賣買人，科有持質，皆非盜事，故分以為《劫略律》。

translations.literal: Robbery law bundled highway seizure, terror extortion, and human trafficking—none purely theft—so Wei spun them into a Pillage fascicle.
translations.idiomatic: Robbery chapters bundled ransom raids and kidnappings—now isolated under Pillage.

sentences.zh: 《賊律》有欺謾、詐偽、逾封、矯制、《囚律》有詐偽生死，《令丙》有詐自復免，事類眾多，故分為《詐律》。

translations.literal: Bandit law mingled fraud, forged orders, feigned deaths, and bogus amnesties—now unified under Fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Assorted frauds migrated from Bandit, Prison, and Decree Bing clauses into one Fraud book.

sentences.zh: 《賊律》有賊伐樹木、殺傷人畜產及諸亡印，《金布律》有毀傷亡失縣官財物，故分為《毀亡律》。

translations.literal: Bandit law also punished tree-felling, livestock slaughter, and lost seals while Metal-Cloth statutes tracked ruined government goods—split into Destruction and Loss.
translations.idiomatic: Environmental and property damage clauses left Bandit law for a Destruction fascicle.

sentences.zh: 《囚律》有告劾、傳覆，《廄律》有告反逮受，科有登聞道辭，故分為《告劾律》。

translations.literal: Prison law listed accusation, forwarding, and review; Stables law listed counter-reports and rearrests; statutes covered roadside petitions—now combined under Accusation.
translations.idiomatic: Litigation mechanics scattered across Prison and Stables chapters merged into Accusation.

sentences.zh: 《囚律》有系囚、鞫獄、斷獄之法，《興律》有上獄之事，科有考事報讞，宜別為篇，故分為《系訊》、《斷獄律》。

translations.literal: Binding prisoners, interrogation, and verdict chapters overlapped Rise-law jail deliveries and appellate commands—now separated into Binding-and-Interrogation and Trial fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Custody, interrogation, and trial stages finally earned distinct fascicles.

sentences.zh: 《盜律》有受所監受財枉法，《雜律》有假借不廉，《令乙》有呵人受錢，科有使者驗賂，其事相類，故分為《請賕律》。

translations.literal: Robbery statutes punished bent judges; Miscellaneous statutes punished questionable loans; Decree Yi punished verbal shakedowns; envoys faced bribery audits—merged under Soliciting Bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Corruption clauses scattered across Robbery, Miscellaneous, and Decree Yi united under Soliciting Bribes.

sentences.zh: 《盜律》有勃辱強賊，《興律》有擅興徭役，《具律》有出賣呈，科有擅作修舍事，故分為《興擅律》。

translations.literal: Robbery statutes punished insulting bandits; Rise statutes punished illegal corvée; Completing statutes tracked unauthorized budgets—all folded into Unauthorized Rise.
translations.idiomatic: Labor abuses and insult cases jumped into Unauthorized Rise.

sentences.zh: 《興律》有乏徭稽留，《賊律》有儲峙不辨，《廄律》有乏軍之興，及舊典有奉詔不謹、不承用詔書，漢氏施行有小愆之反不如令，輒劾以不承用詔書乏軍要斬，又減以《丁酉詔書》，《丁酉詔書》，漢文所下，不宜復以為法，故別為之《留律》。

translations.literal: Rise statutes punished withheld labor; Bandit statutes punished supply failures; Stables statutes punished logistics breakdowns; older canons punished disrespecting edicts—Han practice equated minor slips with capital military guilt until Emperor Wen's Dingyou edict softened the rule; because Dingyou was ad hoc, Wei carved a dedicated Detention fascicle.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée delays, supply bungles, and edict disputes had been jammed into mismatched chapters; Wei isolated detention crimes once accidental overlap with capital military guilt was unwound.

sentences.zh: 秦世舊有廄置、乘傳、副車、食廚，漢初承秦不改，後以費廣稍省，故後漢但設騎置而無車馬，則律猶著其文，則為虛設，故除《廄律》，取其可用合科者，以為《郵驛令》。

translations.literal: Qin maintained relay barns, post riders, escort wagons, and kitchens; early Han copied them until costs forced cuts—Later Han kept only mounted relays, leaving obsolete stable clauses hollow; Wei deleted Stables law and folded surviving courier rules into a Post and Relay decree.
translations.idiomatic: Obsolete Qin-Han relay statutes became a Post-Relay decree once horse relays alone survived budget cuts.

sentences.zh: 其告反逮驗，別入《告劾律》。

translations.literal: Counter-rebellion reporting and rearrest verification moved into Accusation law.
translations.idiomatic: Treason reporting stayed with the new Accusation fascicle.

sentences.zh: 上言變事，以為《變事令》，以驚事告急，與《興律》烽燧及科令者，以為《驚事律》。

translations.literal: Palace memorials on emergencies became Changing-Matters decrees; urgent alarms paired Rise-law beacon rules into Alarm-Matters statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Emergency memorials and beacon alarms gained paired decree chapters.

sentences.zh: 《盜律》有還贓畀主，《金布律》有罰贖入責以呈黃金為價，科有平庸坐贓事，以為《償贓律》。

translations.literal: Robbery law governed restitution to victims; Metal-Cloth law priced fines in gold; average embezzlement rules merged into Restitution.
translations.idiomatic: Restitution tracking moved from Robbery and Metal-Cloth codes into one fascicle.

sentences.zh: 律之初制，無免坐之文，張湯、趙禹始作監臨部主、見知故縱之例。

translations.literal: Original codes lacked exemption-from-accessory rules until Zhang Tang and Zhao Yu invented supervisory knowing-and-conniving precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Accessory liability crystallized once Zhang Tang and Zhao Yu defined supervisory complicity.

sentences.zh: 其見知而故不舉劾，各與同罪，失不舉劾，各以贖論，其不見不知，不坐也，是以文約而例通。

translations.literal: Knowing accomplices who refuse impeachment share guilt; negligent non-impeachment pays redemption; unknowing overseers escape punishment—text stays lean yet examples interconnect.
translations.idiomatic: Clear knowledge triggered joint guilt, negligent oversight triggered fines, ignorance meant innocence—concise yet flexible.

sentences.zh: 科之為制，每條有違科，不覺不知，從坐之免，不復分別，而免坐繁多，宜總為免例，以省科文，故更制定其由例，以為《免坐律》。

translations.literal: Statute commands once listed incidental violations piecemeal; Wei unified exemption exemplars into Exemption-from-Sitting law to thin redundant text.
translations.idiomatic: Repeating accessory exemptions cluttered each chapter, so Wei centralized them.

sentences.zh: 諸律令中有其教制，本條無從坐之文者，皆從此取法也。

translations.literal: Whenever orders teach doctrine but root articles omit accessory rules, judges cite the exemption fascicle.
translations.idiomatic: Silent statutes now defer to the consolidated exemption chapter.

sentences.zh: 凡所定增十三篇，就故五篇，合十八篇，於正律九篇為增，于旁章科令為省矣。

translations.literal: Thirteen new fascicles plus five surviving originals yield eighteen—more than Han's nine roots yet leaner than side decrees.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen streamlined fascicles replace sixty Han scrolls plus piles of side edicts.

sentences.zh: 改漢舊律不行于魏者皆除之，更依古義制為五刑。

translations.literal: Obsolete Han clauses incompatible with Wei vanished; punishments realigned with classical five-punishment theory.
translations.idiomatic: Wei stripped unenforceable Han residue and mapped penalties onto classical five-scale doctrine.

sentences.zh: 其死刑有三，髡刑有四，完刑、作刑各三，贖刑十一，罰金六，雜抵罪七，凡三十七名，以為律首。

translations.literal: Capital offenses subdivided into three grades; shaved-head punishments four; intact and labor punishments three each; redemption eleven; cash fines six; miscellaneous offsets seven—thirty-seven named penalties forming the statutory head.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-seven listed punishments—three capital modes, four shaving grades, paired labor scales, eleven redemption steps, six fines, seven offsets—anchor the code.

sentences.zh: 又改《賊律》，但以言語及犯宗廟園陵，謂之大逆無道，要斬，家屬從坐，不及祖父母、孫。

translations.literal: Bandit law now treats speech crimes and temple-tomb sacrilege as Great Treason warranting waist-cutting; kin guilt excludes grandparents and grandchildren.
translations.idiomatic: Verbal lese-majeste and tomb desecration trigger waist-cutting while collateral guilt spares grandparents and grandkids.

sentences.zh: 至於謀反大逆，臨時捕之，或汙瀦，或梟菹，夷其三族，不在律令，所以嚴絕惡跡也。

translations.literal: Plotting rebellion invites field punishment—bogging, displaying corpses, clan extinction—left outside written statutes to dramatize horror.
translations.idiomatic: Live rebellion draws extrajudicial clan extinction beyond codified sentences.

sentences.zh: 賊鬥殺人，以劾而亡，許依古義，聽子弟得追殺之。

translations.literal: Brawl homicides who flee indictment may be hunted by sons or younger brothers under revived vendetta rights.
translations.idiomatic: Family revenge against fugitive killers regained classical sanction.

sentences.zh: 會赦及過誤相殺，不得報仇，所以止殺害也。

translations.literal: Amnesties and accidental killings block blood revenge to curb vendetta cycles.
translations.idiomatic: General amnesties and mutual accidents end revenge rights to stop feuds.

sentences.zh: 正殺繼母，與親母同，防繼假之隙也。

translations.literal: Deliberate killing of a stepmother matches birth-mother treatment—closing loopholes for sham step relations.
translations.idiomatic: Murdering a stepmother now equals matricide to prevent fake household splits.

sentences.zh: 除異子之科，使父子無異財也。

translations.literal: They removed the statute on differential estates among sons so fathers and sons no longer held separate property.
translations.idiomatic: Deleting the rule that split heir estates kept parental wealth undivided.

sentences.zh: 歐兄姊加至五歲刑，以明教化也。

translations.literal: Striking elder siblings had punishment raised to five-year labor in order to clarify moral teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Assault on older siblings now drew five years’ penal labor to underscore ethical hierarchy.

sentences.zh: 囚徒誣告人反，罪及親屬，異于善人，所以累之使省刑息誣也。

translations.literal: When convicts falsely accused others of rebellion, guilt extended to relatives, differing from honest plaintiffs—thereby burdening them so they checked torture and halted malicious suits.
translations.idiomatic: Malicious jailhouse denunciations dragged kin into guilt—extra deterrence meant to curb torture and perjury.

sentences.zh: 改投書棄市之科，所以輕刑也。

translations.literal: They changed the article exposing anonymous placards to marketplace execution in order to lighten punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Publishing sedition posters no longer automatically earned immediate marketplace execution.

sentences.zh: 正篡囚棄市之罪，斷凶強為義之蹤也。

translations.literal: They corrected marketplace sentences for prisoners seized in breakout—the tracks of labeling brute rescuers as righteous champions.
translations.idiomatic: Storming jails to free captives received clearer labeling instead of heroic loopholes.

sentences.zh: 二歲刑以上，除以家人乞鞫之制，省所煩獄也。

translations.literal: For punishments of two years labor or more they abolished the rule letting kin petition for rehearing—thereby sparing clogged prisons.
translations.idiomatic: Serious labor sentences dropped redundant family appeals that flooded dockets.

sentences.zh: 改諸郡不得自擇伏日，所以齊風俗也。

translations.literal: They revised law so commanderies could no longer pick their own dog-day rituals—thereby harmonizing local customs.
translations.idiomatic: Local jurisdictions stopped selecting independent "dog-day" amnesty dates.

sentences.zh: 斯皆魏世所改，其大略如是。

translations.literal: These represent Wei-era revisions—their gist was as stated.
translations.idiomatic: Wei jurists adopted roughly these headline reforms.

sentences.zh: 其後正始之間，天下無事，於是征西將軍夏侯玄、河南尹李勝、中領軍曹羲、尚書丁謐又追議肉刑，卒不能決。

translations.literal: Later in the Zhengshi era the realm was peaceful—thereupon General Who Conquers the West Xiahou Xuan, Intendant of Henan Li Sheng, Central Army Commander Cao Xi, and Minister Ding Mi again debated corporal punishment yet never resolved it.
translations.idiomatic: During carefree Zhengshi years Xiahou Xuan, Li Sheng, Cao Xi, and Ding Mi reopened the corporal-punishment quarrel without closure.

sentences.zh: 其文甚多，不載。

translations.literal: The documents were extremely numerous and are not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Debate records ran too long for inclusion.

sentences.zh: 及景帝輔政，是時魏法，犯大逆者誅及已出之女。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing acted as regent, Wei law still executed married-away daughters for fathers’ great-treason convictions.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sima Shi co-rule, daughters married out still died for parental treason.

sentences.zh: 毋丘儉之誅，其子甸妻荀氏應坐死，其族兄顗與景帝姻，通表魏帝，以匄其命。

translations.literal: At Guanqiu Jian’s execution his son Dian’s wife Lady Xun faced collateral death; her clansman Yan, tied by marriage to Emperor Jing, memorialized the Wei emperor begging mercy.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanqiu Jian fell, Dian’s wife Lady Xun faced execution until cousin Xun Yan’s plea reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔聽離婚。

translations.literal: An edict permitted divorce.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial writ sanctioned divorce to spare her.

sentences.zh: 荀氏所生女芝，為潁川太守劉子元妻，亦坐死，以懷妊系獄。

translations.literal: Lady Xun’s daughter Zhi, wife of Yingchuan prefect Liu Ziyuan, also faced death; pregnant, she was detained.
translations.idiomatic: Her pregnant daughter Zhi, wed to Prefect Liu Ziyuan, awaited execution under guard.

sentences.zh: 荀氏辭詣司隸校尉何曾乞恩，求沒為官婢，以贖芝命。

translations.literal: Lady Xun pled before Colonel Director of Retainers He Zeng, begging to become an official bondmaid to redeem Zhi’s life.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xun offered herself as government slave to ransom Zhi.

sentences.zh: 曾哀之，使主簿程咸上議曰：「夫司寇作典，建三等之制；

translations.literal: He Zeng pitied her and ordered aide Cheng Xian to memorialize: "When the Minister of Justice forged canons he framed three-tier scales;
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng had Cheng Xian argue:

sentences.zh: 甫侯修刑，通輕重之法。

translations.literal: Marquis Fu polished punishments, threading light and heavy sentences."
translations.idiomatic: Fu marquis tuned statutes linking lighter and graver penalties.

sentences.zh: 叔世多變，秦立重辟，漢又修之。

translations.literal: Late ages shifted endlessly—Qin devised cruel executions; Han piled more atop.
translations.idiomatic: Every dynasty reworked Qin-Han severity.

sentences.zh: 大魏承秦漢之弊，未及革制，所以追戮已出之女，誠欲殄丑類之族也。

translations.literal: Great Wei inherited Qin-Han abuses before systemic overhaul—so tracing punishment to married-away daughters aimed to exterminate villainous kin.
translations.idiomatic: Wei still copied harsh collateral rules to stamp out traitorous houses.

sentences.zh: 然則法貴得中，刑慎過制。

translations.literal: Yet law prizes proportionality; punishments must fear crossing limits.
